findings.rootCause: HashJoinIteration's contract-aware constructor opened both inputs unguarded (`this.leftIter = left.evaluate(bindings); this.rightIter = right.evaluate(bindings);`). A QueryEvaluationException from the second call propagates before the object exists, so handleClose() can never run and the left input (and its store cursor / LMDB reader slot) leaks. All production callers (JoinQueryEvaluationStep, LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep sub-select hash path, BoundedHashJoinIteration, FedX) use this constructor.
findings.change: New private static openRightInput(leftIter, right, bindings): opens the right input inside try/catch(RuntimeException|Error); on failure closes the left input, attaches a close failure as suppressed (guarding against the same instance), and rethrows the original failure. Roadmap 4.7's fully lazy opening is left as a follow-up (it changes close-before-first-next semantics); this is the minimal root-cause fix the design prescribes.

findings.rootCause: MinusQueryEvaluationStep passed the operator's full input BindingSet to the right operand (DelayedEvaluationIteration(rightQes, bindings) on the streaming path and rightQes.evaluate(parentBindings) in AdaptiveMinusIteration.initialize). For `?s :p ?z OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y MINUS { ?y :r ?z } }` the correlated LeftJoinIterator hands {s,z} to the Difference; z is pre-bound in `?y :r ?z` although z is not in the MINUS comparison domain ({y}), so the RHS is a selection on a variable that is fresh under bottom-up semantics and nothing is removed. comparisonBindingNames (shared output names) was already correct; only the pushed input was wrong.
findings.change: MinusQueryEvaluationStep now derives `rightInputBindingNames` and evaluates the right operand with BindingScopeAnalysis.retain(bindings, rightInputBindingNames) on all three paths (SPARQLMinusIteration delayed right, AdaptiveMinusIteration materialized and spilled). The pushed set is (comparison names ∩ rightArg.getAssuredBindingNames()) ∪ BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(rightArg): pushing a shared name is only a selection when the operand binds it in every row (critique 3.4.2 minor; a non-assured name re-extended by BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator would let the operand's own !BOUND filter see a value bottom-up never produces). The restriction applies only where correlated rows can arrive: BindingScopeAnalysis.receivesCorrelatedInput(difference) is true iff the Difference is (inside) the right arg of a Join/LeftJoin/Lateral/Difference and not inside an EXISTS body (which substitutes the probe row). A top-level MINUS keeps receiving all external bindings, which RDF4J treats as constants in the whole query; the existing QueryJoinOptimizerAdversarialTest#directMinusPreservesIncomingBindingRequiredByRhsService pins that contract (SERVICE endpoint bound from outside) and went red under the unconditional restriction from the interrupted attempt, so this position check is the regression fix. Legacy constructors without a comparison domain keep full pushdown (self-consistent: they also compare on all names).

findings.rootCause: Both failing compliance ids are the query `?s ex:predicate ?o LATERAL { OPTIONAL { SELECT * { ?s rdfs:label ?label } LIMIT 1 } }`. The LATERAL right arg is LeftJoin(SingletonSet, Slice(Projection)); LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.supply computed optionalVars = {s,label} (SingletonSet has no binding names to subtract) and the branch-added whenWellDesigned wrapper routed every input binding s to BadlyDesignedLeftJoinIterator, which evaluates the sub-select WITHOUT s, LIMIT 1 returns the store's first label, the row is rejected as incompatible for the other subjects and no bare row is emitted: 1 row instead of 3. Under LATERAL substitution semantics the substituted names are constants in the whole right-hand side and can never be badly-designed problem variables; the step had no way to know that, and LateralQueryEvaluationStep's runtime clone of the right arg had no parent chain at all. Two adjacent defects in the same step: the sub-select hash branch never published its algorithm name (explain showed null), and the OPTIONAL condition was scoped to leftJoin.getBindingNames() so `LATERAL { OPTIONAL { ?s :q ?y FILTER(?y = ?o) } }` never matched (critique 'missed finding' / 3.4.1 minor).
findings.change: BindingScopeAnalysis.lateralSubstitutedNames(node) walks the parent chain, collects Lateral.getRightInputBindingNames() whenever the node is inside a Lateral's right arg and filters them through intervening Projection/MultiProjection source names. LateralQueryEvaluationStep.prepareRight gives the renamed clone a synthetic `new Lateral(new SingletonSet(), scopedRight, rightInputBindingNames)` parent before precompiling it. LeftJoinQueryEvaluationStep.supply removes the substituted names from optionalVars (so isWellDesignedFor ignores them and the sub-select goes through the existing HashJoinIteration branch with s bound, the pattern case through LeftJoinIterator), the sub-select hash branch now sets leftJoin.setAlgorithm(HashJoinIteration), and the condition scope is leftJoin.getBindingNames() ∪ lateralSubstitutedNames (conditionScopeBindingNames). The static-vs-runtime divergence the critique notes (declared but unbound-in-this-row names) is documented in the Javadoc: intersecting with assured left names would wrongly drop optional-but-bound left names and break LATERAL semantics, and a per-row set would have to be threaded through every operator; the divergent case only arises when an operator enclosing the whole LATERAL correlates such a name, which is that operator's responsibility.
